# init:service

[Docs](../README.md) · CLI scaffolding

Bootstraps a complete microservice project from scratch.

## Usage

```sh
mkdir catalog && cd catalog
go mod init catalog
waffle init:service
```

The command takes no operands: it reads the module path from `go.mod`, so the
module has to exist first. The last segment of that path is the service name and
also becomes a Go package name in `api/`, so it has to be a plain identifier —
`catalog`, not `my-service`.

## Generated files

### Entry point

**`cmd/app/main.go`**

The binary entry point. Calls `config.Init()` which resolves the DI container and wires the closer:

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"
    "mymodule/config"
)

func main() {
    application, err := config.Init()
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("failed to start: %s\n", err)
        os.Exit(1)
    }
    application.RunUntilStop()
}
```

### Configuration wrapper

**`config/config.go`**

A thin wrapper that delegates to the diogen package:

```go
package config

import (
    "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/app"
    "mymodule/config/diogen"
)

func Init() (app.App, error) {
    return diogen.InitDi()
}
```

### DI registrations

DI configuration lives in two files inside `config/di/`:

**`config/di/modules.go`** — the set of waffle modules this service composes. Contains **only** blank imports, no other code. `_ "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/config/app"` must always be present — it registers the application root that collects all `Command` tags.

```go
// Composition of waffle modules used by this service.
package di

import (
    _ "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/config/app"
    _ "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/config/service/pry"
    // ... other modules ...
)
```

**`config/di/di.go`** — the `//go:generate` directive and `InitDi()` with service-specific wiring:

```go
//go:generate go tool diogen -output config/diogen/di_gen.go $GOFILE
package di

// import "gitlab.com/gorib/di" // uncomment when adding di.Wire / di.Define calls below

func InitDi() {
	// service-specific di.Wire / di.Define calls go here
}
```

The logger and the rest of the infrastructure arrive with the modules in `modules.go`.

Each tool page shows the exact block to copy inside `InitDi()` when you need manual control. Example for the HTTP tool:

```go
di.Wire[server.Mux](server.New)
session := di.Define(middleware.NewSession)
// ... the rest of the standard middlewares ...
di.Wire[whttp.Global](whttp.NewGlobal, di.Fallback(), di.Args(map[string]any{
    "layers": di.List(compress, health, session /* ... */),
}))
di.Wire[app.BaseCommand](
    func() app.BaseCommand { return app.NewCommand("http", "Start web server") },
    di.For[whttp.HttpCommand](),
)
di.Wire[whttp.HttpCommand](whttp.NewHttpCommand, di.Tag(app.CommandTag), di.Args(map[string]any{
    "routers": di.Tags(whttp.RouterTag),
}))
```

### Diogen adapter

**`config/diogen/di.go`**

Hand-written adapter between the generated container and the application. Calls `InitApp()` (generated), wires the closer, and returns `app.App`:

```go
package diogen

import "gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/app"

func InitDi() (app.App, error) {
    di, err := InitApp()
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    application := di.AppApp()
    if closable, ok := application.(app.HasCloser); ok {
        closable.SetCloser(di.Shutdown())
    }
    return application, nil
}
```

**`config/diogen/di_gen.go`**

Generated DI container. **Do not edit.** Regenerated by `make generate` every time you change DI registrations in `config/di/di.go`.

### API initialization

**`api/init.go`**

Empty initialization file for the service API package. Add HTTP route registration and gRPC handler registration here.

**`api/proto/.gitignore`**

Ensures the `proto/` directory is tracked by git even when empty.

### Project files

**`waffle.yaml`**

Project-level conventions the generators read instead of hardcoding paths.
`init:service` writes all three — `api_import`, `proto_dir` and `mapper` —
each with its default and a comment saying what it decides. What a component
test may replace is not among them: that is `replacements.allow` in specrig's
`specrig.yaml`. A missing file behaves exactly like one holding only the
defaults, so the file is documentation as much as configuration. Keys in
[CLI overview](overview.md#waffleyaml).

**`.env`**

Local environment variable overrides for development. Loaded automatically by `gitlab.com/gorib/env` on startup. Not committed to git.

It starts nearly empty on purpose: a variable arrives with the module that reads
it, and a module arrives with the scaffolding command that needs it. `init:service`
writes no `DAEMON_HOST` because nothing listens yet.

**`.gitignore`**

Standard Go gitignore plus `.env`.

**`waffle`**

A one-line script running `go tool waffle`, so `make generate` and anything
else in the repository calls the version pinned in `go.mod` rather than whatever
is on the developer's `PATH`.

**`Makefile`**

Standard targets:

| Target | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `make generate` | Run all code generators (DI, store), then write `waffle.md` |
| `make .tidy` | `go mod tidy` |
| `make test` | `go test ./...` — before a commit, and in CI |
| `make build` | Build the binary into `bin/` |
| `make run ARGS=<command>` | `.tidy generate`, then `go run ./cmd/app <command>` |
| `make audit` | `golangci-lint run` |
| `make all` (the default) | `.tidy generate build` |

`run` tidies and regenerates first — the same pair every scaffolding command
runs — so a new import or a new registration is in the binary that starts. The
subcommand goes in `ARGS` because make reads a bare word as a target of its own.

**`test` is deliberately out of `all`.** A bare `make` is what runs after every
edit, and the component suite boots the real container over real infrastructure
— too slow for that loop. `make test` belongs before a commit and in CI.

The consequence is worth knowing, because a check rides in that suite:
`boundaries.Check()` sits in `config/diogen`, so a green `make` says the service
builds, not that the domain boundaries are clean.

## Post-generation steps

After writing all files, `init:service` runs:

```sh
go get -tool gitlab.com/gorib/di/cmd/diogen@<di version waffle was built with>
go get -tool gitlab.com/gorib/waffle/cmd/waffle@<its own version>
make .tidy generate
```

Both versions come from the binary, so the service starts on the generator and
the waffle that scaffolded it, not on whatever was released since. A waffle
built from a checkout carries no version anyone can fetch and installs
`@latest`.

This installs the DI code generator, puts `waffle` behind the scaffolded `./waffle` script that `make generate` calls, and produces the initial `diogen/di_gen.go` so the project compiles immediately. It also writes `waffle.md` with the current framework conventions for AI coding agents, and an `AGENTS.md` that brings it in (+ symlinks `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules`) — see [agents](agents.md).

## Keeping waffle.md in sync

After every waffle upgrade (`go get gitlab.com/gorib/waffle@latest`) run:

```sh
waffle agents
```

This rewrites `waffle.md` with the conventions of the new waffle version. Commit the diff. `waffle.md` is fully waffle-managed — hand edits are lost on regeneration; `AGENTS.md` is the service's own.

## What to do next

A fresh service registers no commands at all, so `go run ./cmd/app --help` lists
none — every command arrives with a module, and a module arrives with the
scaffolding command that needs it.

1. `waffle make:domain <domain>` — the first domain, and with it the database modules; `make generate` refuses it until step 2
2. `waffle make:domain:http <domain>` or `make:domain:grpc` — a transport, which reads the domain and puts a command in the list
3. Both of those enable their modules in `modules.go` and append the variables they read to `.env`; the per-module list is [Running locally](../reference/running-locally.md)
4. `make generate` after every DI change — `make run ARGS=<command>` does it for you

[Getting Started](../getting-started.md) walks that path end to end, from here to
a route answering `curl`.
